good.say: a good idea · be good at · have a good day
ex: Is this cafe good?
Have a good day!
That is a good idea.
Anna is a good teacher.

please.say: Yes, please · please + verb: Please sit down

nice.say: Nice to meet you · have a nice day
ex: Nice to meet you.
Have a nice day!
Is the weather nice today?
Anna is very nice.

fight.say: watch a fight · win a fight · have a fight
ex: Is the fight on TV today?
Can we watch the fight?
Anna wins the fight.
The big fight is at nine.

stuff.say: my stuff · a lot of stuff
stuff.note: Informal and uncountable: say "a lot of stuff", not "stuffs".

ex: Your new phone is cool!
Is this jacket cool?
Cool! See you at six.
Look at this cool car!
cool.note: Informal word for "very good". It can also mean a little cold.

hair.say: long/short hair · cut your hair · wash your hair
ex: Anna has long hair.
Can you cut my hair?
Is my hair OK?
I wash my hair every day.
hair.note: Uncountable: say "her hair is long", not "her hairs are long".

support.note: Most often "support" means help: "Thank you for your support."

request.say: make a request · send a request · a friend request

ex: I will remember this day forever.
We can't stay here forever.
Do you want to live here forever?
Will you love me forever?

sale.say: on sale · a big sale · for sale
sale.note: Also means selling: "for sale" = you can buy it. "On sale" = at a lower price.

item.say: an item on the list · items in your cart
ex: How much is this item?
Each item costs five dollars.
I have ten items in my cart.
You can buy new items in the game.
Online dating is very popular now.
Do you use a dating app?
Dating can be hard in a new city.
He made a profile on a dating site.

radio show.say: listen to a radio show · on a radio show
ex: I listen to a radio show every morning.
She hosts a music radio show on Fridays.
What time does the radio show start?
Can we call the radio show?

fix.say: a quick fix · a bug fix
fix.note: Most often "fix" is a verb, to repair: "Can you fix my bike?"

video file.say: open a video file · send a video file
ex: The video file is too big to email.
Save the video file on your computer.
I can't open this video file on my phone.
Can you send me the video file?

fail.say: an epic fail · a total fail
fail.note: Most often "fail" is a verb: "I failed the test." The noun "fail" is internet slang.

ex: The setting of the movie is a small town.
The story has a beautiful village setting.
What is the setting of this book?
The game has a dark fantasy setting.
setting.note: Often "settings" on a phone: "Open the settings." Also the place where something happens.

sport club.say: join a sport club · go to a sport club
ex: My son goes to a sport club after school.
Our town has a new sport club.
Is there a sport club near here?
The sport club has a big swimming pool.

coffee shop.say: at a coffee shop · meet at the coffee shop

shopping center.say: at the shopping center · go to the shopping center
ex: We went to the shopping center on Saturday.
The shopping center opens at nine.
There is a movie theater in the shopping center.
Is the shopping center far from here?

squad.say: join a squad · in our squad
squad.note: Also a group of soldiers or police: "a police squad." Informally, your group of friends.

video chat.say: have a video chat · video chat with

mood.say: in a good/bad mood · in the mood for
ex: I'm in a good mood today.
He is in a bad mood this morning.
Music always changes my mood.
Are you in the mood for pizza?

invite.say: get an invite · send an invite
invite.note: Most often "invite" is a verb: "Can I invite Anna to the party?" The noun is informal.

fighter.say: a professional fighter · a fighter jet
ex: He is a professional fighter.
The two fighters shook hands before the match.
Is your brother a good fighter?
The young fighter won his first fight.
fighter.note: Can also mean a military plane, "a fighter jet," or a soldier.

alert.say: get an alert · a weather alert
alert.note: Often an adjective: "Stay alert" means watch carefully.

fact-check.say: do a fact-check · run a fact-check

R&B.say: listen to R&B · an R&B singer

service center.say: take it to a service center

extra time.say: go into extra time · in extra time
extra time.note: In soccer, mostly British; Americans say "overtime". Also just "more time": "I need extra time."

sold out.say: be sold out · a sold-out show
sold out.note: Before a noun, use a hyphen: "a sold-out show".

travel show.say: watch a travel show · host a travel show

life coach.say: see a life coach · work with a life coach

video content.note: Usually uncountable: "more video content", not "video contents".

green card.say: get a green card · apply for a green card

high score.say: beat your high score · get a high score

ex: My business partner and I opened a cafe together.
Choose your business partner very carefully.
I'm meeting a new business partner for lunch today.
Is your business partner also your friend?

food blog.say: write a food blog · on a food blog

talent show.say: at the talent show · win a talent show

tour agent.note: "Travel agent" is the more common word.

fake news.say: spread fake news · spot fake news
fake news.note: Uncountable: "a piece of fake news", not "a fake news".

travel blog.say: write a travel blog · read a travel blog

live chat.say: use live chat · on live chat

red flag.say: a big red flag · ignore the red flags

info center.note: "Information center" is the full and more formal form.

radio signal.say: send a radio signal · lose the radio signal

golf club.note: Can also mean the stick used to hit the ball.
